description: Rank invoices the same way, and return every invoice ranked in the top 10, including all invoices tied at 10th place.

a.request: For each invoice, together with its customer's country, compute the average `UnitPrice` of its invoice lines. Take the overall average of these invoice averages, and for each invoice compute its deviation (invoice average minus overall average). Then, for each country, average these deviations over its invoices. For each invoice, show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and that deviation minus its country's average deviation. Sort by this last value from highest to lowest (blanks last) and return the top 10, including every invoice tied with the 10th one. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId, c.Country AS Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), d AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), e AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country_avg FROM d), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL), dev_minus_country_avg DESC) AS rk FROM e) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, dev_minus_country_avg FROM r WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY (dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL), dev_minus_country_avg DESC

c.request: Work out each invoice's average line `UnitPrice` (with its customer's country) and how far that is from the average across all invoices. Which are the top 10 invoices whose deviation sits furthest above their country's average deviation? Show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and the deviation minus the country's average deviation, sorted highest first (blanks last) and unrounded. Rank invoices the same way, and return every invoice ranked in the top 10, including all invoices tied at 10th place.
c.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), cd AS (SELECT *, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country FROM dev), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (dev_minus_country IS NULL), dev_minus_country DESC) AS rnk FROM cd) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, dev_minus_country FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY (dev_minus_country IS NULL), dev_minus_country DESC, InvoiceId

b.request: Rank invoices by how far their deviation from the overall average of per-invoice average line UnitPrice exceeds their customer country's average deviation, and return the top 10 by that difference, descending with NULLs last, plus every invoice tied with the 10th-place value, showing invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and deviation minus country average deviation, all unrounded
b.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, avg_unit_price - AVG(avg_unit_price) OVER () AS deviation FROM inv), diff AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country_avg FROM dev), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, dev_minus_country_avg DESC) AS rnk FROM diff) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, dev_minus_country_avg FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY CASE WHEN dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, dev_minus_country_avg DESC, InvoiceId

d.request: Work out each invoice's average line `UnitPrice` (with its customer's country) and how far that is from the average across all invoices. Rank the invoices by how far their deviation sits above their country's average deviation, and return every invoice ranked in the top 10, including all invoices tied at 10th place. Show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and the deviation minus the country's average deviation, sorted highest first (blanks last) and unrounded.
d.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - AVG(avg_price) OVER () AS deviation FROM inv), d2 AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country_avg FROM dev), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL), dev_minus_country_avg DESC) AS rnk FROM d2) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, dev_minus_country_avg FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY (dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL), dev_minus_country_avg DESC, InvoiceId
